source: One Year Prayer Cycle for the Diocese of Georgia for 2026
sourceFile: "OneYearPrayerCycle2026.pdf", fetched directly from https://gaepiscopal.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/OneYearPrayerCycle2026.pdf, linked from the diocese's own Diocese of Georgia Prayer Cycle page at https://gaepiscopal.org/diocese-of-georgia-prayer-cycle/.
notes: The diocese's own web page (https://gaepiscopal.org/diocese-of-georgia-prayer-cycle/) offers two distinct cycles: a day-of-month (1-31) “Diocese of Georgia Prayer Cycle” list embedded directly in the page (also offered as a printable PDF, and as a separate clergy-spouses variant), and a linked “One Year Prayer Cycle for the Diocese of Georgia for 2026” PDF (https://gaepiscopal.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/OneYearPrayerCycle2026.pdf) explicitly “for use in weekly worship,” organized as 52 dated Sunday-anchored weeks. This file transcribes the latter, since it is the diocese's actual Sunday-by-Sunday cycle matching this corpus's other diocese-level 'dated' files; the day-of-month list is a separate product of the same diocese and is not transcribed here.

The source labels each week by a Sunday-Saturday date range (e.g. “December 28 - January 3”) rather than a single date. Per this corpus's convention of one date per entry, `date` records the first day of that range (the Sunday), which is also the day the week's Prayers of the People would actually be used. Every one of the 52 ranges was confirmed to begin on a Sunday and run exactly 7 days.

Week 1's range (“December 28 - January 3”) begins Sunday, December 28, 2025, not in calendar year 2026, because the diocese's 52-week grid starts on the last Sunday of the prior December rather than on January 1. This is transcribed as printed, not an error or a gap; the file's `year` field (2026) records the calendar year this “One Year Prayer Cycle for 2026” document as a whole is titled/published for, per this corpus's per-year filing convention.

Each week's source text is prose, not a directory list, and names three distinct layers of prayer: (1) the Diocese of Georgia's own congregations/bishops/offices (“In our diocesan cycle of prayer…”), (2) that week's local ecumenical partner congregations of other traditions (“We also pray for our ecumenical partners…”), and (3) named congregations/institutions of the companion Diocese of the Dominican Republic (“In our companion diocese of the Dominican Republic…”). Only layer (1)'s actual Georgia congregations are recorded as `parish` subjects (with `place` = the city/town as given); bishops, diocesan offices/programs, ecumenical-partner congregations, and companion-diocese congregations/institutions are all recorded as `category` subjects, since the schema's `place` field is defined only for `parish` subjects — for these, the source's own contextual framing (the city/town given, “ecumenical partner,” “Catholic”/“Lutheran,” “companion diocese of the Dominican Republic,” and any Spanish-language parenthetical translation) is preserved in that subject's own `note` field instead. Grammatical framing immediately surrounding a name in the source's prose (e.g. “we pray for our congregation in Albany,” or “especially”) is not itself transcribed as part of any subject's `name`.

Where the source capitalizes a leading “The” as part of a name printed mid-sentence (e.g. “…and The Church of the Resurrection Lutheran Church,” “we pray for The Ascension (La Ascensión)”), that capital “The” is kept as part of the transcribed `name`. Where the source instead uses a lowercase “the” as ordinary sentence grammar (e.g. “…especially, the Church of the Atonement”, “our congregation in Vidalia, the Church of the Annunciation”), that grammatical article is dropped from `name` (e.g. “Church of the Atonement”, “Church of the Annunciation”) rather than transcribed, since it is not part of how the source capitalizes the name itself.
Diocese's own full name transcribed exactly as printed on the source PDF and the diocesan website: “Episcopal Diocese of Georgia” (no leading “The”).

Week 18's ecumenical-partner sentence (“our ecumenical partners in the Catholic churches in Cuthbert and Donalsonville—St. Luke's and the Church of the Incarnation”) names two cities and two churches but never states which church is in which city; both subjects' `note` fields disclose this rather than guessing a pairing.

Week 2's source PDF text carries a stray space before a comma in “St. John & St. Mark’s ,” — a PDF text-layer extraction artifact, not a printed character, so it was not preserved literally; the name is transcribed as “St. John & St. Mark’s”.

Apparent typos/oddities in the source, preserved verbatim rather than silently corrected: Week 12's “Holy Word (Verbo Divina)” (Spanish grammar would expect “Verbo Divino”); Weeks 22 and 26 both print “Apostól” with the accent on the wrong syllable (elsewhere in the same document, Weeks 2, 32, and 46, the same word is correctly printed “Apóstol”); Week 23's “The Encarnation (La Encarnación)” (the expected English word is “Incarnation”); Week 34's “St. Barthlomew (San Bartolomé)” (expected “Bartholomew”); Week 35's “The Good Samartian (El Buen Samaritano)” (expected “Samaritan”); Week 37's “San Pedro de Marorís” (likely intended “San Pedro de Macorís”, by comparison with Week 35's “San Francisco de Macorís”); Week 38 names the same congregation “St. Matthew” in English but “(San Matías)” in Spanish, which actually translates to “St. Matthias”, not “St. Matthew” — an apparent English/Spanish name mismatch in the source itself; Week 41's “The Annunciation (La Annunciación)” (standard Spanish spelling is “La Anunciación”, one “n”); Week 49 prints a lowercase “our Lady of the Assumption Catholic Church” (likely intended “Our”); Week 4's companion-diocese place name is printed “Banî” (circumflex), likely intended “Baní” (acute accent, the standard spelling of this Dominican Republic town); Week 50's “Holy Trinity (Santísma Trinidad)” (standard Spanish spelling is “Santísima”). Week 18 also prints “St. Luke's” with a plain/straight apostrophe — the only such instance anywhere in the document, every other apostrophe being the curly ’ form — preserved exactly as printed rather than normalized to match the rest of the file.

Week 51's “our Episcopal Campus Ministries at Augusta, Valdosta State, and Georgia Southern Universities” is recorded as a single `category` subject (“Episcopal Campus Ministries”) covering all three universities, since the source does not present three separately named ministries.
